clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad synced currency census widened (L-872): 20 windows of 2,000 blocks from deployment to block 125342320, every transaction with a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer from or to the PoolManager traced with callTracer and replayed against the transient model of src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I chose this item because a wrong clearance here would hide a settle credited from another transaction's sync, which is a direct path to other users' funds. I rebuilt the transaction list of window 7 (blocks 64,655,420 to 64,657,419) myself on https://rpc.monad.xyz. I used eth_getLogs in spans of 100 blocks for PoolManager logs and for ERC-20 Transfer topics with the PoolManager as sender or receiver. That gave 256 transactions, the same set as raw/m143/logs-7.json, with none missing and none extra. I then traced transaction 0xc1439a64... (block 105,113,079, picked with seed 'verify-143' from the rows with a settle check) with debug_traceTransaction and the callTracer. Its PoolManager frames were unlock, sync, settle, swap, two exttload and two take, none reverted, which is the frame list census.jsonl records. The model the census applies matches the code. sync stores the currency and the balance, or resets for native (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). _settle pays msg.value when nothing is synced, reverts on msg.value when an ERC-20 is synced, pays balance minus reserves, and resets (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). I did not recompute the settle amounts of the 14,234 checks. The census is evidence about mined history only. That transient storage clears between transactions on Monad rests on the earlier client source reading in OPCODES.md, not on this item.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Silent log gap check (L-881) on the endpoints behind earlier censuses of chain 999 (HyperEVM): eth_getLogs of PoolManager Swap and ModifyLiquidity logs compared with the PoolManager logs in each endpoint's own receipts, plus a known-block check of 40 blocks from the 2,782 transaction census list.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I chose this item because the HyperEVM census of all 2,782 transactions rests on these endpoints, and HyperEVM has a closed producer. The topic hashes in gapcheck2.py:17 equal keccak of the Swap and ModifyLiquidity signatures in src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:78-100. I checked them with web3_sha3 on forno.celo.org. On https://rpc.purroofgroup.com and https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, blocks 50,592,430 and 51,109,618 each gave 1 log by getLogs and 1 by receipts. Receipts equal the transaction count on each endpoint (6 and 10). The window 51,109,331 to 51,110,330 gave 4 logs on purroofgroup. On the official endpoint it failed loudly with 'execution aborted (timeout = 5s)', as the item says. Block 0x2bdddef has the same hash on both endpoints. purroofgroup lists 7 transactions and the official endpoint lists 5. The two left out have gasPrice 0, and one of them is sent from 0x2000000000000000000000000000000000000000, a system sender. So the item is right that the official endpoint hides HyperCore system transactions. System transactions come first in the block and run as transactions of their own, so they cannot land between one user's sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). At most they leave the PoolManager unclaimed surplus, which is the F-137 pattern.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Which client produces Celo mainnet blocks today (L-877). The item concludes celo-reth, and the clearances L-245, L-256 and L-343 rest on that.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I chose this item because three earlier clearances depend on which client produces Celo blocks. https://forum.celo.org/t/celo-mainnet-is-now-running-op-reth/13594 (HTTP 200, CeloCoreCo, 22 July 2026) says Celo Mainnet runs op-reth and that op-geth nodes 'will not be able to follow the canonical chain'. I read https://github.com/celo-org/op-geth/pull/509 through Exa web fetch, because curl got HTTP 403. It was merged 2026-08-18, and it says block 75046581 index 29 (0xe9e0248c...) was processed by celo-reth and rejected by op-geth, that 'the block is canonical', and that 'the lenient rule is still live in the sequencer'. On forno, eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex(0x4791eb5, 0x1d) returned that hash with type 0x7b, fee currency 0x0e2a3e05..., gas 0x30d40 and maxFeePerGas 0x6c65312b3. Their product is 5,819,427,363,800,000, which matches the pull request. Two web3_clientVersion calls on forno returned reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb. One correction: the pull request gives the sender's balance as 5,295,000,000,000,000, which is the figure the item says it could not reproduce. That figure is not needed for the conclusion. I did not rerun the 200 height hash comparison.
